- Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods of the 30-day forecast, especially after sharp spikes or volatility.
- Overestimates in the middle to late forecast horizon, particularly when history shows mean reversion or downward momentum.
- Tends to overshoot after recent price spikes, then corrects too slowly — lagged correction in the 10–15 day window.
- Underestimates when true outcome shows strong mean reversion toward lower levels, especially after high peaks.
- Overconfident in short-term momentum; fails to account for seasonal or policy-driven corrections (e.g., EU ETS cap adjustments).
- Often ignores recent low-levels in history when forecasting, leading to persistent underestimation of downward trends.
- Forecast bias is more pronounced in the first 5–7 days; later days show more alignment with true values, suggesting model adjusts after initial lag.
- When history includes a recent high followed by a drop, model tends to overcorrect downward, then undercorrects later — creating a “double dip” error pattern.
